stem: Which of the following carbanions is the strongest base?

verdicts.working: Alkyl groups donate electron density by the +I effect, destabilizing a carbanion. Basicity therefore increases with substitution: CH₃⁻ < primary < secondary < tertiary.

working:
$+I$ effect of alkyl groups destabilises the carbanion; basicity increases with alkyl substitution: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^- > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^- > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^- > \text{CH}_3^-$.

Independent check: Alkyl groups donate electron density by the +I effect, destabilizing a carbanion. Basicity therefore increases with substitution: CH₃⁻ < primary < secondary < tertiary.
solution:
The $+I$ effect of alkyl groups destabilizes a carbanion, increasing its basicity with substitution:
$$\text{CH}_3^- < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^- < (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^- < (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$$
Thus, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$ is the strongest base.
